provenance: G24 approved adaptive foundation; current MFRS-V1.1 question bank plus approved pathway structure.

responseScale.label: Not in place
responseScale.operationalMeaning: The control, process or capability does not exist or is not recognised as required.

responseScale.label: Initial / ad hoc
responseScale.operationalMeaning: Some activity may occur informally or reactively, but it is not defined, owned or reliable.

responseScale.label: Partially designed
responseScale.operationalMeaning: Some elements exist, but implementation is incomplete, inconsistent or not evidenced.

responseScale.label: Implemented
responseScale.operationalMeaning: The capability is established in important areas, but may not operate consistently across the organisation.

responseScale.label: Consistently operating
responseScale.operationalMeaning: The capability is formally implemented, evidenced and regularly operating.

responseScale.label: Embedded and improved
responseScale.operationalMeaning: The capability is monitored, measured, governed and continuously improved.

domains.name: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
Continuous Improvement and Fraud Risk Monitoring

gateways.prompt: What best describes your organisation’s primary operating model?
Approximately how many people work in the organisation?
Does your organisation use external suppliers or contractors?
How is procurement or buying handled?
Does your organisation handle physical cash?
Does your organisation hold physical stock, inventory or valuable equipment?
Does your organisation sell online or accept digital or card payments?
Does your organisation hold personal information about customers, clients or employees?
Does your organisation process refunds, credit notes or manual adjustments?
Does the organisation operate from more than one site, store or project location?
Does your organisation use temporary, seasonal or subcontracted workers?
Do employees work remotely or do you depend on third-party digital platforms?
Who approves payments and significant spending?

gatewayBlocks.title: About your organisation
gatewayBlocks.intro: Short operating-model questions establish applicability before the scored domains.

gatewayBlocks.title: Before fraud-risk identification
gatewayBlocks.intro: Operating-model context determines which risk-identification pathways apply.

gatewayBlocks.title: Before operational controls
gatewayBlocks.intro: Money, stock, people and manual-activity context determines operational applicability.

gatewayBlocks.title: Before supplier and procurement controls
gatewayBlocks.intro: Supplier, procurement and payroll context determines direct versus retained-governance questions.

questions.prompt: A named senior owner is accountable for fraud risk management and has authority to drive action.
questions.controlObjective: Give one senior executive explicit authority and accountability for fraud-risk decisions.

questions.prompt: Fraud risk is recognised in the organisation's wider risk or governance framework.
questions.controlObjective: Carry fraud risk as a named risk inside the organisation-wide risk and governance framework rather than as an informal concern.

questions.prompt: Fraud risks, incidents and control weaknesses are reported to senior leadership or a governance forum on a defined rhythm.
questions.controlObjective: Give leadership a predictable, evidence-based view of fraud exposure, incidents and control weaknesses.

questions.prompt: Management owns fraud risk, while internal audit or assurance functions provide independent review where they exist.
questions.controlObjective: Separate management ownership of fraud risk from independent assurance over that ownership.

questions.prompt: The organisation has written fraud guidance, policies or procedures explaining how fraud should be prevented, detected, reported and managed.
questions.controlObjective: Put the organisation’s fraud rules in writing so expected behaviour and required process are not left to individual interpretation.

questions.prompt: Leadership receives updates on emerging fraud threats affecting the sector, operating model or customer and supplier environment.
questions.controlObjective: Keep leadership informed of fraud threats actually emerging in the sector, operating model and counterparty base.

questions.prompt: The organisation has completed a structured fraud risk assessment within the past two years.
questions.controlObjective: Establish a current, structured and documented view of where the organisation is actually exposed to fraud.

questions.prompt: Fraud risks have been mapped across important processes such as procurement, payments, refunds, claims, stock, supplier management or service delivery.
questions.controlObjective: Map fraud risk to the specific operational processes where value can actually be diverted.

questions.prompt: New systems, channels, products, services or operational changes include fraud-risk review before implementation.
questions.controlObjective: Force a fraud-risk review into the design of new systems, channels, products, services and operational changes before they go live.

questions.prompt: Fraud risks are refreshed when the organisation changes how it operates, serves customers or works with suppliers.
questions.controlObjective: Keep the fraud risk picture aligned to how the organisation currently operates rather than how it operated when the assessment was written.

questions.prompt: Fraud risks linked to suppliers, contractors, agents, intermediaries or other third parties have been assessed.
questions.controlObjective: Assess the fraud risk introduced by suppliers, contractors, agents, intermediaries and other third parties acting for or with the organisation.

questions.prompt: The organisation monitors emerging fraud threats affecting its industry, geography or operating environment.
questions.controlObjective: Track fraud threats emerging in the organisation’s own industry, geography and operating environment and convert them into control questions.

questions.prompt: The organisation considers how fraud could occur through misuse of authority, privileged access, approvals, system permissions or operational process gaps.
questions.controlObjective: Consider deliberately how insiders could misuse authority, privileged access, approvals, system permissions or process gaps.

questions.prompt: The organisation considers how fraud could occur through customer or user platforms, online forms, WhatsApp journeys, loyalty programmes, service portals or other digital channels where relevant.
questions.controlObjective: Assess fraud risk arising through customer and user digital channels where the organisation operates them.

questions.prompt: High-risk processes have segregation of duties between initiation, approval, processing and reconciliation.
questions.controlObjective: Ensure no single person can initiate, approve, process and reconcile the same high-risk transaction.

questions.prompt: Transactions or operational activities above defined risk or value thresholds require independent review or approval.
questions.controlObjective: Require genuinely independent review or approval for transactions and activities above defined risk or value thresholds.

questions.prompt: Supplier onboarding includes checks on business information, ownership, banking details or other fraud-risk indicators.
questions.controlObjective: Prevent fictitious, conflicted or misrepresented suppliers from entering the approved vendor population.

questions.prompt: System and data access are granted based on role requirements and reviewed periodically.
questions.controlObjective: Keep ordinary system and data access aligned to current job responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Sensitive manual activities such as refunds, credits, write-offs, stock adjustments, manual journals or overrides are monitored or reviewed.
questions.controlObjective: Bring sensitive manual adjustments under independent review because they bypass normal transactional controls.

questions.prompt: Operational processes are periodically reviewed to identify control weaknesses or opportunities for manipulation.
questions.controlObjective: Periodically re-examine operational processes for control weaknesses and manipulation opportunities that have emerged in practice.

questions.prompt: People in high-risk roles are subject to appropriate oversight, rotation, secondary review or other compensating controls.
questions.controlObjective: Apply proportionate oversight to roles whose authority, access or custody creates elevated fraud opportunity.

questions.prompt: The organisation monitors transactions or operational activity for unusual patterns, anomalies or red flags.
questions.controlObjective: Actively monitor transactions and operational activity for unusual patterns, anomalies and red flags.

questions.prompt: Exception reports or alerts highlighting unusual transactions or activities are generated and reviewed regularly.
questions.controlObjective: Ensure generated fraud and control exceptions are actually investigated and resolved.

questions.prompt: Analytics, rules, reports or data checks are used to identify suspicious transactions, behaviour or control exceptions.
questions.controlObjective: Use analytics, rules, reports or data checks to surface suspicious transactions, behaviour and control exceptions.

questions.prompt: Detection controls are updated when new fraud risks, fraud methods or operational changes emerge.
questions.controlObjective: Keep detection controls current as fraud methods, risks and operations change.

questions.prompt: Monitoring covers both internal misuse and external fraud threats where these are relevant to the organisation.
questions.controlObjective: Cover both internal misuse and external fraud threats within the monitoring design.

questions.prompt: People responsible for monitoring suspicious activity know when to escalate concerns and have authority to do so.
questions.controlObjective: Ensure monitoring staff know when to escalate and hold the authority to do so without obstruction.

questions.prompt: Detection controls are periodically reviewed for effectiveness by management, risk, audit or another independent reviewer.
questions.controlObjective: Independently test whether detection controls are actually working, not merely running.

questions.prompt: The organisation has a documented process for responding to suspected fraud incidents.
questions.controlObjective: Create a repeatable, coordinated response to suspected fraud.

questions.prompt: Employees know where and how to report suspected fraud or misconduct.
questions.controlObjective: Make sure every employee knows exactly where and how to report suspected fraud or misconduct.

questions.prompt: Roles and decision rights are defined for fraud triage, investigation, escalation and closure.
questions.controlObjective: Define who decides what at each stage of fraud triage, investigation, escalation and closure.

questions.prompt: Fraud investigations follow procedures that protect confidentiality, fairness, evidence and documentation.
questions.controlObjective: Conduct investigations so that confidentiality, fairness and documentary integrity are protected throughout.

questions.prompt: Evidence linked to suspected fraud is identified, preserved and handled appropriately.
questions.controlObjective: Identify, preserve and account for fraud evidence so integrity and provenance can be demonstrated.

questions.prompt: External specialists are considered when incidents require forensic, legal, cyber or investigative expertise.
questions.controlObjective: Bring in specialist forensic, legal, cyber or investigative capability when a case exceeds internal capability.

questions.prompt: Lessons from fraud incidents are used to improve controls and reduce repeat exposure.
questions.controlObjective: Convert what each incident reveals into control improvements that reduce repeat exposure.

questions.prompt: The organisation provides a confidential or anonymous channel for reporting suspected fraud or misconduct.
questions.controlObjective: Provide a safe, confidential route for internal and relevant external fraud concerns.

questions.prompt: Employees know how to use the whistleblowing or confidential reporting channel.
questions.controlObjective: Ensure the workforce actually knows how to use the confidential reporting channel, not merely that one exists.

questions.prompt: Reports submitted through the channel are reviewed independently from the people or teams implicated.
questions.controlObjective: Guarantee that reports are assessed independently of the people or teams they implicate.

questions.prompt: The organisation clearly communicates that retaliation against whistleblowers or people who raise concerns is prohibited.
questions.controlObjective: State and enforce that retaliation against people who raise concerns is prohibited.

questions.prompt: Reporting channels are accessible to relevant external stakeholders such as suppliers, contractors, customers or beneficiaries where appropriate.
questions.controlObjective: Extend reporting access to external stakeholders who observe misconduct the workforce cannot see.

questions.prompt: Employees receive guidance or training on recognising and reporting suspicious behaviour.
questions.controlObjective: Equip employees to recognise the behavioural and situational signals that should prompt a report.

questions.prompt: Suppliers, contractors or other third parties are subject to due diligence before being engaged.
questions.controlObjective: Risk-screen every supplier, contractor or third party before engagement.

questions.prompt: Procurement processes include safeguards against collusion, manipulation, bid rigging or favouritism.
questions.controlObjective: Protect competitive sourcing from collusion, manipulation, bid rigging and favouritism.

questions.prompt: Employees are required to disclose and manage conflicts of interest involving suppliers or third parties.
questions.controlObjective: Surface and actively manage employee conflicts of interest involving suppliers and third parties.

questions.prompt: Supplier payment processes include checks to reduce invoice manipulation, fake vendors, bank-detail changes or vendor impersonation.
questions.controlObjective: Prevent invoice manipulation and fraudulent vendor bank-detail changes before payment release.

questions.prompt: High-risk suppliers or third-party relationships are periodically monitored or reviewed.
questions.controlObjective: Keep high-risk third-party relationships under periodic review after onboarding, not only at the point of engagement.

questions.prompt: Procurement or vendor-management activity is subject to oversight or periodic review.
questions.controlObjective: Subject procurement and vendor-management activity itself to oversight, since it controls both supplier selection and payment eligibility.

questions.prompt: Fraud risks are considered when using agents, brokers, distributors, intermediaries, partners or outsourced service providers where relevant.
questions.controlObjective: Address the specific fraud risks created by agents, brokers, distributors, intermediaries and outsourced providers acting on the organisation’s behalf.

questions.prompt: The organisation verifies the identity of customers, users, employees, suppliers or counterparties where identity misuse could create fraud loss or harm.
questions.controlObjective: Verify the identity of customers, users, employees, suppliers and counterparties wherever identity misuse could create loss or harm.

questions.prompt: Systems or digital platforms are monitored for suspicious activity such as unusual login, access, profile, transaction or account behaviour.
questions.controlObjective: Detect suspicious login, account, access and transaction behaviour on digital platforms.

questions.prompt: Employees receive training on phishing, social engineering and digital impersonation attempts.
questions.controlObjective: Prepare employees to recognise and resist phishing, social engineering and digital impersonation.

questions.prompt: Access to sensitive digital systems, administrator rights and confidential data is restricted and reviewed.
questions.controlObjective: Restrict and independently recertify privileged, administrator and sensitive-data access.

questions.prompt: Digital activity is monitored for misuse, unauthorised transactions, suspicious data changes or channel abuse.
questions.controlObjective: Detect misuse, unauthorised transactions, suspicious data changes and digital-channel abuse.

questions.prompt: Employees and users know how to report suspicious digital activity or account-security concerns.
questions.controlObjective: Give employees and users a fast, known route to report suspicious digital activity or account-security concerns.

questions.prompt: Emerging digital fraud risks relevant to the organisation's operations or sector are reviewed periodically.
questions.controlObjective: Periodically reassess emerging digital fraud risks relevant to the organisation’s operations and sector.

questions.prompt: The organisation can detect or investigate identity misuse, account takeover, impersonation or unauthorised profile changes where relevant.
questions.controlObjective: Be able to detect and investigate identity misuse, account takeover, impersonation and unauthorised profile changes.

questions.prompt: Employees receive periodic training or guidance on fraud risks relevant to their roles and the organisation's operating environment.
questions.controlObjective: Equip staff to recognise and act on fraud risks specific to their roles.

questions.prompt: Fraud awareness is included in employee onboarding or induction.
questions.controlObjective: Establish fraud expectations at the point of joining, before habits and local practice form.

questions.prompt: Leadership communicates clear expectations on ethical conduct, conflicts of interest and fraud prevention.
questions.controlObjective: Have leadership set explicit, repeated expectations on ethical conduct, conflicts and fraud prevention.

questions.prompt: Employees understand the consequences of fraudulent, dishonest or unethical behaviour.
questions.controlObjective: Ensure employees understand the actual consequences of fraudulent, dishonest or unethical behaviour.

questions.prompt: The organisation uses real examples, scenarios or lessons learned to help employees recognise fraud risks.
questions.controlObjective: Use real examples, scenarios and lessons learned so staff recognise fraud as it actually presents.

questions.prompt: Employees have safe ways to raise concerns and believe those concerns will be taken seriously.
questions.controlObjective: Build genuine confidence that raising a concern is safe and will be taken seriously.

questions.prompt: The organisation periodically reviews its fraud risks and control environment.
questions.controlObjective: Periodically re-examine the fraud risk profile and the control environment as a whole rather than only at incident time.

questions.prompt: Fraud incidents or control failures are analysed to understand root causes and control weaknesses.
questions.controlObjective: Analyse incidents and control failures to understand why they were possible, not merely what happened.

questions.prompt: Lessons from investigations or incidents are translated into control, process, training or monitoring improvements.
questions.controlObjective: Translate lessons from investigations and incidents into actual changes in controls, process, training or monitoring.

questions.prompt: The organisation monitors fraud trends affecting its sector, geography, customer environment or supplier base.
questions.controlObjective: Monitor fraud trends affecting the organisation’s sector, geography, customer environment and supplier base.

questions.prompt: Fraud risk is considered when new systems, products, services, processes or operational changes are implemented.
questions.controlObjective: Ensure fraud risk is considered whenever new systems, products, services, processes or operational changes are implemented.

questions.prompt: Leadership periodically reviews whether key fraud controls remain effective, resourced and fit for purpose.
questions.controlObjective: Have leadership periodically confirm that key fraud controls remain effective, adequately resourced and fit for purpose.

oversightVariants.prompt: Supplier management is outsourced; the organisation retains assurance over provider vetting and due diligence.
oversightVariants.displayGuidance: Outsourcing moves the activity, not the accountability; assess the retained governance control.

oversightVariants.prompt: The organisation defines and monitors the third-party vetting standard applied on its behalf.
oversightVariants.displayGuidance: Outsourcing moves the activity, not the accountability; assess the retained governance control.

oversightVariants.prompt: The organisation retains controls over supplier selection, price integrity and conflict disclosure where procurement is outsourced.
oversightVariants.displayGuidance: Outsourcing moves the activity, not the accountability; assess the retained governance control.

oversightVariants.prompt: The organisation independently verifies supplier banking changes before provider-executed payments are released.
oversightVariants.displayGuidance: Outsourcing moves the activity, not the accountability; assess the retained governance control.

oversightVariants.prompt: The organisation reviews fraud, dispute and account-security reporting from the third-party platform it uses.
oversightVariants.displayGuidance: Outsourcing moves the activity, not the accountability; assess the retained governance control.

oversightVariants.prompt: The organisation independently reviews an externally processed payroll register for unknown, duplicate or altered records.
oversightVariants.displayGuidance: Outsourcing moves the activity, not the accountability; assess the retained governance control.

skipReasonCodes.gateway_no_high_risk_handling: No relevant cash, stock, refund, adjustment or temporary-worker exposure was confirmed.
skipReasonCodes.gateway_no_digital_footprint: No relevant online, digital-payment or platform dependency was confirmed.
skipReasonCodes.gateway_no_digital_or_identity_footprint: No relevant digital channel or personal-information exposure was confirmed.
skipReasonCodes.gateway_no_employee_base: No employee base beyond the owner was confirmed.
skipReasonCodes.upstream_answer_changed: An upstream gateway answer changed the active pathway.
